value.description:
Rice (kome). Edible rice after the husks have been removed. AMJGrains uses one ingredient for both brown and white rice in cooking and milling.

White rice became popular in Edo's urban diets, but white-rice-heavy diets with too few side dishes led to beriberi, called "Edo wazurai" (Edo sickness). Rural households often mixed rice with barley or other grains. Eating plentiful white rice became widely attainable only after postwar economic growth.

In the Meiji period, naval physician Kanehiro Takaki compared the voyages of the warships Ryūjō and Tsukuba and showed that improved diets reduced beriberi. This was an important epidemiological and nutritional finding before the cause was identified. The Army and Navy later suffered greatly different levels of beriberi during the Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese wars.

In 1910, Umetaro Suzuki discovered oryzanin, a beriberi-preventing substance from rice bran later linked to vitamin B1.
